Hi Joe — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few concrete asks so we can keep procurement moving: 

1) SOC 2 / compliance status
- You mentioned BlueWard is SOC 2 Type II in-progress with a planned 2028 audit. Can you confirm which controls (CC2/CC3) are in scope for the systems that will access PHI?

2) Pen test and sharing expectations
- From the security discovery, you asked whether we can share a pen-test report and what redaction looks like. Our standard approach: we can share an executive summary and issue table with CVE-like IDs redacted, and provide a detailed technical report under an NDA and limited distribution.

3) Vulnerability SLAs and scan cadence
- Typical Redwood recommendations for an enterprise integration: 7 days for Critical, 30 days for High, 90 for Medium, vendor-managed timeline for Low. We also run quarterly automated scans plus an annual third-party pentest unless customer requests otherwise.

Next steps I propose:
- Maya (you) to return the attached security questionnaire (column comments are fine) by Wed 5/26.
- If you want the full pen-test report under NDA, confirm the list of people who should receive it and we’ll route to legal.
- Karthik, can you advise on whether the 7/30/90 SLA profile is negotiable for healthcare customers?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up if that helps.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Neha — thanks for the recap, this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- SOC 2: we are currently SOC 2 Type I (infra & change mgmt) and targeting Type II by Q3 2028. Our PHI-handling services are in a separate (restricted) environment and we need to see the specific controls mapping before we can accept the Type II timeline as sufficient.

- Pen test: we absolutely require the full technical report for our security review team, but we can execute an NDA and a short dissemination list. Will need to confirm internal reviewers — I expect 3 people (Security Lead, Head of Compliance, and our Eng manager).

- SLA expectations: the 7/30/90 split makes sense. For Criticals we push to 72 hours for remediation or a documented mitigation plan. Can Redwood support a 72-hour critical timeline for integrations handling PHI?

Maya will take the questionnaire and get it back to you by 5/26. Also looping Priyom for the pen-test NDA flow.

Joe — Priyom from Redwood's security team here. Appreciate the quick reply and the 3-person distribution note — that works. A few operational details on our side so you can prep internal reviewers: 

- NDA & report delivery: we will send a two-way mutual NDA and, once executed, provide the technical report as a password-protected PDF via a secure transfer link. We default to a 7-day hold period after the report is issued before public disclosure to allow coordinated remediation and CVE assignment. If BlueWard requires a shorter embargo for Criticals, we can discuss case-by-case.

- Remediation SLAs: Redwood can commit to 72-hour acknowledgement and mitigation planning for confirmed Critical issues affecting the integration surface, and a 30-day target for High severity fixes where feasible. We log and track all findings in a shared Jira project (read-only for customers) for transparency.

- Scan cadence: automated external scans every quarter, internal dev-scans weekly. For customers in healthcare (PHI scope) we recommend monthly authenticated scans for the integration endpoints.

I'll attach a short guidance doc — see Redwood-PT-Share-Guidance-v1.pdf — that describes redaction practice and the delivery workflow.

If that alignment works, Neha — can you get the NDA template over to Joe and Maya so we can move the report?

—Priyom
